L709: ###### Lemma 3.13.
L710: 
L711: Let $f_{i}:\mathbb{R}\rightarrow[-\infty,\infty)$ ($i\in I$) be a monotone net of proper usc concave functions and $f:\mathbb{R}\rightarrow[-\infty,\infty)$ another proper usc concave function. Assume that $f_{i}(\tau)\to f(\tau)$ for all $\tau\in\mathbb{R}$. Then
L712: 
L714: Recall the definition of $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\theta)$ from Definition 【66†3.3】. When $\{\theta\}=c_{1}(L)$ for some pseudoeffective $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundle $L$ we now define the map:
L715: 
L716:  | $$\textup{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\theta)\ni\phi\mapsto\phi^{\mathrm{an}}\in\textup{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{an}}).$$  |  | (39)
L717: Let $\phi=\{\{\phi^{\omega}_{\tau}\}_{\tau}\}_{\omega\in\mathcal{K}}\in\textup{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\theta)$. Let $\omega\in\mathcal{K}$ be such that $\{\omega\}=c_{1}(T)$, for a $\mathbb{Q}$-ample line bundle $T$. We get that $\{\phi^{\omega}_{\tau}\}_{\tau}\in\textup{MTC}_{\mathcal{I}}(\theta+\omega)$, hence $(\phi^{\omega})^{\mathrm{an}}\in\textup{PSH}((L+T)^{\mathrm{an}})$ by Theorem 【153†3.12】(i). We make the following preliminary definition:
L718:  | $$\phi^{\mathrm{an}}:=(\phi^{\omega})^{\mathrm{an}}.$$  |  | (40)
L719: 
L720: Among other things, we need to show that this definition is independent of the choice of $\omega.$ Let $\omega^{\prime}\in\mathcal{K}^{\prime}$ such that $\{\omega^{\prime}\}=c_{1}(T^{\prime})$, for some $\mathbb{Q}$-ample line bundle $T^{\prime}$ and $\omega\leq\omega^{\prime}$. Then we have that
L721: 
L722:  | $$P_{\theta+\omega^{\prime}}[\phi^{\omega}_{\tau}]_{\mathcal{I}}=\phi^{\omega^{\prime}}_{\tau},\ \ \ \ \tau<\tau^{+}_{\phi}.$$  |
L723: As a result, using [【77†DX22】, Proposition 2.18(ii)], we get that $(\phi^{\omega}_{\tau})^{\mathrm{an}}=(\phi^{\omega^{\prime}}_{\tau})^{\mathrm{an}},\ \tau<\tau^{+}_{\phi}$. Comparing with (【123†24】), we arrive at $(\phi^{\omega})^{\mathrm{an}}=(\phi^{\omega^{\prime}})^{\mathrm{an}}$, as desired.
L724: Moreover, our above analysis also shows that $\phi^{\mathrm{an}}\in\bigcap_{L^{\prime}}\mathrm{PSH}((L+L^{\prime})^{\mathrm{an}})$, where $L^{\prime}$ runs over all ample $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundles on $X$. The latter space is equal to $\mathrm{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{an}})$ by [【42†BJ21】, Theorem 4.5], so our map $\phi\mapsto\phi^{\mathrm{an}}$ from (【160†40】) is indeed well-defined.
L725: 
L726: Observe that
L727: 
L728:  | $$\phi^{\mathrm{an}}(v_{\mathrm{triv}})=\tau^{+}_{\phi},$$  |  | (41)
L729: where $v_{\mathrm{triv}}$ denotes the trivial valuation.
L730: 
L731: We show that the map of (【69†39】) is actually a bijection, giving a transcendental interpretation of the non-Archimedean metrics of Boucksom–Jonsson:
L732: ###### Theorem 3.14.
L733: 
L734: Assume that $\{\theta\}=c_{1}(L)$ for some pseudoeffective $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundle $L$. The map of (【69†39】) is a bijection. In addition, let $\phi,\chi\in\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\theta)$. If $\phi^{\mathrm{an}}\leq\chi^{\mathrm{an}}$ then $\phi\leq\chi$.
L735: ###### Proof.
L736: 
L737: By scaling, we may assume that $L$ is a line bundle. We first address the last statement. Let $\phi=\{\{\phi^{\omega}_{\tau}\}_{\tau}\}_{\omega}$ and $\chi=\{\{\chi^{\omega}_{\tau}\}_{\tau}\}_{\omega}$. Given that $\phi^{\mathrm{an}}\leq\chi^{\mathrm{an}}$, Theorem 【153†3.12】(i) gives that $\phi^{\omega}_{\tau}\leq\chi^{\omega}_{\tau},\ \tau\in\mathbb{R},\omega\in\mathcal{K}$, implying that $\phi\leq\chi$. This immediately gives that $\phi\mapsto\phi^{\mathrm{an}}$ is injective.
L738: To address surjectivity, let $\chi\in\textup{PSH}(L^{\mathrm{an}})$. Let $\omega\in\mathcal{K}$ such that $\{\omega\}=c_{1}(T)$ for a $\mathbb{Q}$-ample line bundle $T$. Then $\chi\in\textup{PSH}((L+T)^{\mathrm{an}})$, and by Theorem 【153†3.12】(ii) there exists $\{\phi^{\omega}_{\tau}\}\tau\in\textup{MTC}_{\mathcal{I}}(\theta+\omega)$ such that $(\phi^{\omega})^{\mathrm{an}}=\chi$.
L739: Let $\omega^{\prime}\in\mathcal{K}$ such that $\{\omega^{\prime}\}=c_{1}(T^{\prime})$, for some $\mathbb{Q}$-ample line bundle $T^{\prime}$ and $\omega\leq\omega^{\prime}$. Due to injectivity of $\textup{MTC}_{\mathcal{I}}(\theta+\omega^{\prime})\mapsto\mathrm{PSH}((L+T^{\prime})^{\mathrm{an}})$ we get that $P_{\theta+\omega^{\prime}}[\phi^{\omega}_{\tau}]_{\mathcal{I}}=\phi^{\omega^{\prime}}_{\tau},\ \tau<\tau^{+}_{\phi}$.
L740: For a non-rational form $\omega^{\prime\prime}\in\mathcal{K}$, let $\omega\in\mathcal{K}$ such that $\{\omega\}=c_{1}(T)$ for a $\mathbb{Q}$-ample line bundle $T$ and $\omega\leq\omega^{\prime\prime}$. Then we define
L741: 
L742:  | $$\phi^{\omega^{\prime\prime}}_{\tau}=P_{\theta+\omega^{\prime\prime}}[\phi^{\omega}_{\tau}]_{\mathcal{I}},\ \ \ \tau<\tau^{+}_{\phi}.$$  |
L743: It is immediate to see that the above definition is independent of the choice of $\omega$. We see that $\{\{\phi^{\omega}_{\tau}\}_{\tau}\}_{\omega}\in\textup{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\theta)$, and $\phi^{\mathrm{an}}=\chi$, proving surjectivity. ∎
L744: ###### Remark 3.15.
L745: 
L746: Boucksom–Jonsson’s theory extends to any pseudoeffective $(1,1)$-class $\{\theta\}$ in the Néron–Severi group of $X$ with real coefficients, giving a space of non-Archimedean metrics $\mathrm{PSH}(\{\theta\}^{\mathrm{NA}})$. In this case we still have a canonical identification
L747: 
L748:  | $$\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\theta)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{PSH}(\{\theta\}^{\mathrm{NA}}).$$  |  | (42)
L749: To see this, let $\mathcal{K}^{\prime}$ be the directed set of $(1,1)$-classes $\{\theta^{\prime}\}$ in the Néron–Severi group of $X$ with rational coefficients such that $\{\theta^{\prime}\}-\{\theta\}$ is a Kähler class. Then we have natural identifications
L750:  | $$\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\theta)\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{\theta^{\prime}\in\mathcal{K}^{\prime}}\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\theta^{\prime}),\hskip 10.00002pt\mathrm{PSH}(\{\theta\}^{\mathrm{NA}})\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{\theta^{\prime}\in\mathcal{K}^{\prime}}\mathrm{PSH}(\{\theta^{\prime}\}^{\mathrm{NA}}).$$  |
L751: 
L752: The former follows immediately from our definition, the latter follows from [【42†BJ21】, Section 4.1, (PSH2)]. In particular, (【161†42】) follows from Theorem 【67†3.14】.
L753: Using our analysis we conclude that the envelope conjecture holds in our setting, as confirmed by Boucksom–Jonsson using non-Archimedean methods [【63†BJ22】]:
L754: ###### Corollary 3.16.
L755: 
L756: Conjecture 【71†2.13】 holds for any pseudo-effective $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundle $L$ on $X$.
L757: ###### Proof.
L758: 
L759: Take a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $\theta$ in $c_{1}(L)$. Let $\{\varphi^{i}\}_{i\in I}$ be a bounded from increasing net in $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(L)$. By Theorem 【67†3.14】, $\varphi^{i}=\phi^{i,\mathrm{an}}$ with $\phi^{i}\in\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\theta)$. By the same theorem, $\{\varphi^{i}\}_{i\in I}$ is also an increasing net. Moreover, by (【162†41】),
L760: 
L761:  | $$\sup_{i\in I}\tau^{+}_{\varphi^{i}}<\infty.$$  |
L762: By Theorem 【70†3.4】, we can find $\phi\in\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\theta)$ such that for any $\omega\in\mathcal{K}$, $\phi^{i,\omega}_{\tau}\nearrow\phi^{\omega}_{\tau}$ almost everywhere for any $\tau<\tau^{+}_{\phi}$.
L763: 
L764: We claim that $\phi^{i,\mathrm{an}}$ converges to $\phi^{\mathrm{an}}$.
L765: 
L766: For any fixed $\omega\in\mathcal{K}$, the usc property of the Lelong number [【163†Bou17】, Lemma 2.6] gives
L767:  | $$(\phi^{\omega}_{\tau})^{\mathrm{an}}(v)=\lim_{i}(\phi^{i,\omega}_{\tau})^{\mathrm{an}}(v)\hskip 10.00002pt\text{for }v\in X^{\mathrm{div}},\tau<\tau_{\psi}^{+}.$$  |
L768: 
L769: It follows that
L770: 
L771:  | $$\phi^{\mathrm{an}}(v)=(\phi^{\omega})^{\mathrm{an}}(v)=\sup_{\tau\in\mathbb{R}}((\phi^{\omega}_{\tau})^{\mathrm{an}}(v)+\tau)=\sup_{\tau\in\mathbb{R}}\sup_{i\in I}((\phi^{i,\omega}_{\tau})^{\mathrm{an}}(v)+\tau)=\sup_{i\in I}\phi^{i,\mathrm{an}}(v)$$  |
L772: 
L773: for all $v\in X^{\mathrm{div}}$, finishing the proof. ∎
L774: ### 3.4 The non-Archimedean finite energy space
L775: 
L776: Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $\{\theta\}$ be a big cohomology class on $X$. Let $V=\int_{X}\theta_{V_{\theta}}^{n}$ denote the volume of $\{\theta\}$.
L777: Recall that $\textup{MTC}_{\mathcal{I}}(\theta)$ naturally embeds into $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\theta)$ (【164†29】). For $\{\eta_{\tau}\}_{\tau}\in\textup{MTC}_{\mathcal{I}}(\theta)$ we define the Monge–Ampère energy $I^{\mathrm{NA}}_{\theta}:\textup{MTC}_{\mathcal{I}}(\theta)\rightarrow[-\infty,\infty)$ as
L778:  | $$I_{\theta}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\eta):=I_{\theta}\{\eta_{\tau}\}=\tau^{+}_{\eta}+\frac{1}{V}\int_{-\infty}^{\tau^{+}_{\eta}}\left(\int_{X}\theta_{\eta_{\tau}}^{n}-V\right)\,\mathrm{d}\tau.$$  |  | (43)
L779: 
L780: We extend $I^{\mathrm{NA}}_{\theta}$ to a function on $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\theta)$ by setting it to be $-\infty$ on $\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\theta)\setminus\textup{MTC}_{\mathcal{I}}(\theta)$.
L781: 
L782: We then define the non-Archimedean finite energy space as
L783:  | $$\mathcal{E}^{1,\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta):=\left\{\phi\in\mathrm{PSH}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\theta):I_{\theta}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\phi)>-\infty\right\}\,.$$  |
L784: Since $V\geq\int_{X}\theta_{\eta_{\tau}}^{n}$, for (【165†43】) to be finite $\int_{X}\theta_{\eta_{\tau}}^{n}$ must converge to $V$ as $\tau\searrow-\infty$. By [【108†DDNL18a】, Theorem 2.3] this implies that $\int_{X}\theta_{\eta_{-\infty}}^{n}=V$. Since $\eta_{-\infty}$ is maximal, we obtain that $\eta_{-\infty}=V_{\theta}$, i.e., $\{\eta_{\tau}\}_{\tau}$ is a test curve relative to $V_{\theta}$, whenever $\{\eta_{\tau}\}_{\tau}\in\mathcal{E}^{1,\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta)$.
L785: Similarly, the non-Archimedean $\mathcal{J}$ functional is introduced as
L786: 
L787:  | $$\mathcal{J}_{\theta}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\eta)=\tau^{+}_{\eta}-I_{\theta}^{\mathrm{NA}}(\eta)=\frac{1}{V}\int_{-\infty}^{\tau^{+}_{\eta}}\left(V-\int_{X}\theta_{\eta_{\tau}}^{n}\right)\,\mathrm{d}\tau.$$  |  | (44)
L788: When $\{\theta\}=c_{1}(L)$ for some ample $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundle $L$, it has been pointed out in [【77†DX22】, Theorem 1.1, Theorem 1.2] that our definitions of $\mathcal{E}^{1,\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta)$ and $\mathcal{J}_{\theta}^{\mathrm{NA}},I_{\theta}^{\mathrm{NA}}$ coincide with the ones given in [【42†BJ21】].
L789: In the literature, the space $\mathcal{E}^{1}(L^{\mathrm{an}})$ has not yet been defined for a general big $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundle $L$. Above we gave an analytic definition, but it is desirable to have a purely non-Archimedean/algebraic definition as well.
L790: 
L791: After defining finite energy non-Archimedean spaces, we can finally relate the $\mathcal{I}$-maximal finite energy rays to non-Archimedean potentials, as a direct consequence of Theorem 【74†2.6】:
L792: ###### Theorem 3.17.
L793: 
L794: There is a bijective function $\{\psi_{\tau}\}_{\tau}\mapsto\{\check{\psi}_{t}\}_{t}$, between $\mathcal{R}^{1}_{\mathcal{I}}(X,\theta)$ and $\mathcal{E}^{1,\mathrm{NA}}(X,\theta)$. Moreover, under this correspondence, the radial Monge–Ampère energy corresponds to the non-Archimedean Monge–Ampère energy defined in (【165†43】).
L795: ## 4 Approximations of $\mathcal{I}$-maximal rays by filtrations and flag configurations
L796: 
L797: In this section $X$ is a connected projective manifold of dimension $n$. The purpose of this section is to show that an $\mathcal{I}$-maximal finite energy ray can be approximated by simpler rays induced by flag configurations or filtrations defined below.
L798: ### 4.1 Filtrations of big line bundles
L799: 
L800: For this subsection let $L$ be a big line bundle on $X$ and $h$ be a smooth Hermitian metric. Let $\theta:=-\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\log h$. We set $\vol(L):=\int_{X}\theta_{V_{\theta}}^{n}$. Denote the section ring of $L$ by $R(X,L)$:
L801: 
L802:  | $$R(X,L):=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb{N}}R_{m},\hskip 10.00002ptR_{m}:=H^{0}(X,L^{m}).$$  |
L803: ###### Definition 4.1.
L804: 
L805: By a (bounded left-continuous multiplicative decreasing) filtration $\mathcal{F}$ of the section ring $R(X,L)$, we mean a family of linear subspaces $\{\mathcal{F}^{\lambda}R_{m}\}_{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}}$ of $R_{m}$ for each $m\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
L806: 
L807: (i)$\mathcal{F}^{\lambda}R_{m}\subseteq\mathcal{F}^{\lambda^{\prime}}R_{m}$ whenever $\lambda\geq\lambda^{\prime}$;
L808: 
L809: (ii) $\mathcal{F}^{\lambda}R_{m}=\bigcap_{\lambda^{\prime}<\lambda}\mathcal{F}^{\lambda^{\prime}}R_{m}$;

A birational version of K-stability for big classes (https://arxiv.org/html/2603.25605v1)

L85: We further define a notion of divisorial stability, where one tests stability through convex combinations of divisorial valuations on $X$ (which can be encapsulated into so-called divisorial measures). Our main result proves the following characterisation in our setting, generalising the work of Boucksom--Jonsson^{2}^{2} 2 We emphasise that their work implies that divisorial stability is equivalent to uniform K-stability with respect to models, which we simply call uniform K-stability in our work..
L86: ###### Theorem 1.1.
L87: 
L88: Suppose $X$ is a smooth projective variety, and $L$ is a big line bundle on $X$. Then $(X,L)$ is uniformly K-stable if and only if it is divisorially stable.
L89: Many new technical issues arise in proving this result, in comparison with the ample case. The first step towards proving this result is to establish a non-Archimedean analogue of the Calabi–Yau theorem for big line bundles, as a big counterpart to ample results of Boucksom, Favre and Jonsson [【58†BFJ15】, 【52†BJ22】]; we adapt a recent approach of Witt Nyström [【59†Nys25】], for which it is crucial that we assume $X$ is smooth.
L90: A major difference in our setting, however, is that we do not establish (and do not expect) uniqueness of solutions, due to a lack of strict convexity of the key Monge–Ampère energy functional. This functional is defined through the volume of a big line bundle, for which one can only expect strict convexity properties on the big and nef (or movable) cone. Geometrically, this means we must permit a single divisorial measure to be associated with many test configurations.
L91: The main consequence of this lack of uniqueness relates to the numerical invariants we attach to a divisorial measure. In the ample case, one essentially defines these invariants precisely so that the norm of a divisorial measure agrees with the norm of its associated test configuration, while the $\beta$-invariant of a divisorial measure is defined in such a way that it agrees with the non-Archimedean Mabuchi functional of its associated test configuration.
L92: It is therefore remarkable that it is possible to produce an intrinsic definition of the $\beta$-invariant in such a way that Theorem 【60†1.1】 holds. For this, we prove left differentiability of the norm of a fixed measure as one varies the big line bundle, using convex optimisation results of Danskin [【61†Dan67】]; we do not expect full differentiability.
L93: We emphasise that our resulting notion of the $\beta$-invariant of a divisorial measure is completely explicit, involving the calculation only of integrated volumes of various collections of divisorial valuations, along with the log discrepancy, in line with the approach of [【33†BJ25b】, 【57†MPN25】] rather than the original approach of [【51†BJ23】].
L94: Another important aspect of our proof is to directly relate the Monge–Ampère measure of a test configuration, the volume of an associated filtration of the section ring, and the “integrated volume” of the associated divisorial measure, through a result of independent interest generalising equidistribution results in [【62†BC11】, 【50†BJ25a】] to globally big test configurations; see Theorem 【63†4.10】.
L95: We use Theorem 【60†1.1】 to prove that uniform K-stability of $(X,-K_{X})$ recovers the prior notions introduced in [【41†DR24】, 【42†DZ24】], implying that our notion of uniform K-stability is a natural extension of the existing theory in the anticanonical case.
L96: Our second main result establishes the birational behaviour of uniform K-stability, for which we consider a birational contraction between smooth projective varieties $\pi:Y\dashrightarrow X$. We endow $X$ and $Y$ with big line bundles $L_{X}$ and $L_{Y}$ respectively such that on the pullback to a resolution of indeterminacy $Z$, we have $L_{Y}=L_{X}+E$, for $E$ an exceptional effective $\mathbb{R}$-Cartier divisor.
L97: ###### Theorem 1.2.
L98: 
L99: $(X,L_{X})$ is uniformly K-stable if and only if $(Y,L_{Y})$ is uniformly K-stable.
L100: A special case to which this result applies is when $L_{Y}$ is the pullback of $L_{X}$ to $X$ through a morphism. Perhaps the most important conceptual consequence is in the case where $L_{Y}$ has finitely-generated section ring: in this case, one obtains a birational contraction $\pi:Y\dashrightarrow X$ and an ample line bundle $L_{X}$ on $X$ such that, on a resolution of indeterminacy, $L_{Y}=\pi^{*}L_{X}+E$ for $E$ effective.
L101: Thus, when $L_{Y}$ has finitely generated section ring—and its ample model $(X,L_{X})$ satisfies the hypothesis that $X$ is smooth—uniform K-stability reduces to the ample setting.
L102: This is compatible with the minimal model programme and surrounding moduli theory: when $K_{X}$ is big, taking the canonical model produces a variety with ample canonical class, and Theorem 【64†1.2】 implies that uniform K-stability is unchanged under passage to smooth canonical models (and indeed, in this case proving uniform K-stability of $(X,K_{X})$ directly is straightforward).
L103: In this way, Theorem 【64†1.2】 implies that we have produced the natural extension of uniform K-stability from the ample cone to the big cone.
L104: In line with the third point in our motivation above, Theorem 【64†1.2】 is an algebro-geometric version of the statement that the existence of (a conjectural notion of) singular cscK metrics in big classes is well-behaved under pullbacks and pushforwards. As such, singular cscK metrics in big classes should be abundant, beginning for example with a smooth cscK manifold $(X,L_{X})$ with $L_{X}$ ample.
L105: Theorem 【64†1.2】 further implies that uniform K-stability is a notion defined at the level of $b$-divisors on the Riemann–Zariski space of $X$, as we explain in Section 【30†5.3】. Many fundamental notions of positivity for classes are defined in terms of classes on the Riemann–Zariski space [【49†BFJ09】, 【65†DF22】], which provides the appropriate framework for (asymptotic) birational-geometric questions, and our work thus gives a theory of uniform K-stability that fits into this framework.
L106: We end with a more philosophical comment on our approach to uniform K-stability in the big setting, which is motivated by considerations from non-Archimedean geometry. Boucksom–Jonsson [【52†BJ22】] have given a general theory of plurisubharmonic metrics in non-Archimedean geometry, for arbitrary pseudoeffective classes. Our work is strongly influenced by theirs, but does not use the same approach; our notion of a test configuration is distinct from their notion of a non-Archimedean Fubini–Study metric.
L107: More precisely, in the complex (Archimedean) theory, a plurisubharmonic metric can be viewed as a decreasing limit of (in general singular) Fubini–Study metrics through Demailly approximation [【66†Dem92】], which is taken as a definition in non-Archimedean pluripotential theory.
L108: Our approach is instead motivated by the fact that plurisubharmonic envelopes of continuous functions are dense in the space of metrics with minimal singularities; our test configurations are analogues of such plurisubharmonic envelopes.
L109: In the Boucksom–Jonsson theory, a major issue is that the space of finite energy plurisubharmonic non-Archimedean metrics with minimal singularities is not known to be complete in general, even in the big and nef case (see [【67†DXZ25】] for related results using the formalism of [【68†RN14】]). The approach which we take means we do not require analogous completeness results to obtain a working theory, such as in our approach to the non-Archimedean Monge–Ampère equation.

L111: ## 2. K-stability for big line bundles
L112: 
L113: We will be interested throughout in a smooth complex projective variety $X$ of dimension $n$, with canonical class $K_{X}$. For a big line bundle $L$ on $X$, our aim is to define the pair of conditions that $(X,L)$ be uniformly K-stable and divisorially stable. In subsequent sections, we will prove the equivalence of the two conditions.
L114: ### 2.1. Preliminaries on positivity and volume
L115: 
L116: We begin by recalling the basics of positivity theory in algebraic geometry, referring to Lazarsfeld and Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson for introductions [【69†Laz17】, 【70†Laz04】, 【49†BFJ09】]. In the present section, we assume that $X$ is merely normal.
L117: #### 2.1.1. Positivity of line bundles.
L118: 
L119: We recall that a line bundle $L$ on $X$ is big if its volume
L120: 
L121:  | $$\mathrm{vol}(L):=\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{h^{0}(X,kL)}{k^{n}/n!}$$  |
L122: is strictly positive; it is a classical result that the limit involved in the definition exists. Equivalently, $L$ is big if and only if $L=A+E$ with $A$ ample and $E$ effective on $X$. Bigness can be generalised in the natural way to $\mathbb{R}$-divisors and is a numerical property. In particular, the big cone in $N^{1}(X)$ is open [【69†Laz17】, Corollary 2.2.24]. A line bundle $L$ is pseudoeffective if its numerical class lies in the closure of the big cone.
L123: We say that $L\geq L^{\prime}$ if $L-L^{\prime}$ is pseudoeffective.
L124: Given a line bundle $L$ on $X$, we define its stable base locus $Bs(||L||)=\bigcap_{k>0}Bs|kL|;$ its augmented base locus or non-nef locus $B_{+}(L):=\bigcap_{A}Bs(||L-A||)$, with $A$ varying over all ample $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors on $X$; and its restricted base locus or non-ample locus $B_{-}(L):=\bigcup_{A}Bs(||L+A||)$ with $A$ varying over all ample $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors on $X$.
L125: We have $B_{-}(L)\subseteq B(L)\subseteq B_{+}(L)$; furthermore, $L$ is pseudoeffective if and only if $B_{-}(L)\neq X$, and $L$ is big if and only if $B_{+}(L)\neq X$. Given a divisor $D$, we say a pseudoeffective line bundle $L$ is $D$-pseudoeffective if $D$ is not contained in $B_{-}(L)$, and $D$-big if $D$ is not contained in $B_{+}(L)$ [【49†BFJ09】, Remark 4.2]. Note that the $D$-pseudoeffective cone is the closure of the $D$-big cone, which conversely is the interior of the former.
L126: Given a big line bundle $L$ and a divisor $E$ on $X$, we define the pseudoeffective threshold of $L$ with respect to $E$ as
L127: 
L128:  | $$\gamma(L,E):=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}_{>0},\,L-\gamma E\text{ is big}\}.$$  |
L129: #### 2.1.2. Positive intersection theory.
L130: 
L131: For $L$ a big line bundle on $X$, one defines the positive intersection product as in [【49†BFJ09】, Definition 2.5]:
L132: 
L133:  | $$\langle L^{k}\rangle:=\sup_{D}\,(\pi^{*}L-D)^{k},$$  |
L134: where the supremum (taken in the sense of the pseudoeffectivity partial order $\geq$ as above) ranges over all divisors $D$ in a birational model $\pi:Y\to X$ such that $\pi^{*}L-D$ is nef.
L135: Formally, $\langle L^{k}\rangle$ is viewed as an element of $N^{k}(\mathfrak{X})$, the space of $p$-dimensional Weil classes on the Riemann–Zariski space $\mathfrak{X}$ of $X$ [【49†BFJ09】, Definition 1.1], though we require very little of the general theory (though we refer to Section 【30†5.3】 for a more complete discussion). We note $\langle L^{k}\rangle=\langle L\rangle^{k}$ in the resulting positive intersection theory, and we employ both notations throughout.
L136: The positive intersection product extends to the boundary of the pseudoeffective cone in a natural manner in [【49†BFJ09】, Definition 2.10], and to zero outside the pseudoeffective cone. It is not a continuous extension in general, except in the case where $k=n$.
L137: 
L138: Provided $L$ is big, its volume is computed as a positive intersection product:
L139: 
L140: (2.1)  |  | $$\mathrm{vol}(L)=\langle L^{n}\rangle.$$  |
